source.title: Deep Networks as Logical Circuits: Generalization and Interpretation

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study experimentally examines how architecture size and data structure relate to generalization, using controlled synthetic datasets and a different measure and setting from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites random-label memorization and other prior work but does not test random labels. Its architecture and generalization-gap plots are figure-only; bounds in Table 1 are not direct measurements of the gap.
record.test_reason: The study reports related generalization results but tests none of V1–V8. Its architecture comparison increases depth rather than width beyond an interpolation threshold; its MNIST intervention replaces a circuit component rather than removing memorized examples. Random-label fitting is cited, and magnitude-aware sharpness is not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that structured data constrains learned classifiers, report depth-invariant generalization error in controlled synthetic experiments, and demonstrate one MNIST circuit repair. They also emphasize exact logical-circuit representations and comparatively small capacity bounds, while identifying efficient analysis of higher-dimensional inputs as an open problem.
record.recipe_differences: Controlled experiments use fully connected ReLU networks on synthetic 2D binary data; architecture varies in depth and size. The paper also demonstrates a logical-circuit interpretation and component replacement on MNIST.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset structure and architecture size/depth; the paper reports that the learned decision boundary changes with data complexity, while added depth does not qualitatively change it for a fixed dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors describe generalization error as invariant to increasing depth and architecture size on their synthetic datasets, with qualitatively similar decision boundaries for fixed data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing fully connected network depth can preserve generalization and decision-boundary simplicity on structured synthetic data.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing an identified memorizing circuit component with a separately trained prosthetic improved one MNIST classifier's test accuracy from 0.78 to 0.83.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpreting and replacing a logical-circuit component can improve an already trained classifier's held-out accuracy.

record.problems: The main architecture/generalization-gap results are plots without reported numerical gap values in the text. The controlled experiments use synthetic 2D data and do not test random-label fitting. The MNIST repair is one reported example.
record.rows_left_out: No further claim-relevant results with directly reported outcomes were identified. Capacity bounds and neuron-state counts are not direct measurements of the gap or the properties named in V7.

untested.parts: Own experiments comparing random-label fitting and held-out performance with natural-label training under the same architecture and recipe.
Width scaling beyond the width needed for zero training error and its effect on held-out error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against other measures.
Removal of examples selected by label-memorization influence, retraining, and comparison with equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix 9.3 specifies Adam for the experiments despite the main text's generic gradient-descent wording. Stable generalization gaps under added depth do not establish decreasing test error under added width. Row states are relative to the listed claim versions; the off-claim MNIST accuracy improvement is observed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels, compare random-label and natural-label test accuracy, or evaluate the specified architectures and datasets.
Varies depth and architecture size on synthetic 2D data, not width in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Studies fully connected networks only; does not compare them with convolutional networks.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on the specified benchmarks; controlled experiments use Adam.
Does not vary batch size or compare large- and small-batch training.
Does not test dropout or weight decay.
Compares capacity bounds with the generalization gap in plots, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or the specified norm- and margin-based measures as predictors.
Does not remove memorized training examples and retrain; its MNIST intervention replaces a logical circuit component with a separately trained prosthetic.

rows.subject: ArchI, ArchII, and ArchIII
rows.size_stated: 3, 6, and 9 hidden layers; 107, 517, and 1743 parameters, respectively
rows.operation_detail: Compared generalization gap as architecture size increased on DataIII.

conditions.value: ArchI, ArchII, ArchIII; increasing depth and parameter count

rows.note: The text says depth-invariant generalization error is consistent with Figure 4b, but does not give numerical gap values or describe the individual plotted values.
rows.check: The architectures add layers while retaining the existing layer structure. This does not test V2's width intervention or establish continued test-error reduction beyond the width needed to fit. The text explicitly describes depth-invariant generalization error, although numerical gaps cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: ArchIII network and engineered classifier h(x)
rows.size_stated: ArchIII; the original network also has a 4 neuron linear layer
rows.stage_stated: trained; engineered classifier uses a separately trained prosthetic
rows.operation_detail: Replaced a memorizing component in the logical circuit with a prosthetic classifier trained to label 4 as False and 5–9 as True.

conditions.value: original network uses 1k training points; prosthetic uses m = 250 training samples

rows.note: The authors describe the original network as overfit; this circuit replacement is not the example-removal intervention in V8.
rows.check: The accuracy improvement from 0.78 to 0.83 is correctly recorded, but it measures circuit replacement. No training examples are removed followed by retraining, and there is no matched random-removal control, so it cannot establish V8.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
